problem: Only GET and PUT are named as idempotent, while DELETE is defined in the same paragraph and is also idempotent. A student can conclude that DELETE is not idempotent and lose marks on a method-semantics question.
fix: Say: GET, HEAD, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST (and PATCH) are not. Keep the point that GET is also safe, that is, read-only.

problem: On a miss the 300 KB body crosses two links, origin to edge and edge to browser, but the transfer time of 150 ms is counted only once. The arithmetic is right only if the edge streams the body to the client while receiving it.
fix: State the assumption: the edge streams, so one 150 ms transfer is charged. Otherwise miss latency = 120 + 150 + 150 = 420 ms, average = 0.92×170 + 0.08×420 = 190 ms, and the saving is 80 ms.

where: Section 2, sentence 'The hit ratio decides cost'
problem: Overstated. Cost is decided by bytes served from the origin, which the request hit ratio does not fix; the chapter's own trap says a small hot object raises the request hit ratio without saving much bandwidth.
fix: Say: cost follows the miss traffic in bytes, so the byte hit ratio matters as much as the request hit ratio; the request hit ratio alone can mislead.
